BRACE POSITION
FLIGHT SAFETY
o avoid injury in case of impact, the appro-
priate brace position must be used.
The brace positions should be with the upper
body bent forward as far as possible with the chest
close to the thighs and knees, and the head touch-
ing the seat back in front of you. The hands should
be placed one on top of the other and on top of
the head. Fingers should no be interlocked, the
forearms should be tucked in against each side of
the face, the lower legs should be inclined after
with the feet placed flat on the floor.
Take the brace position when instructed by the
cabin attendants. Remain in the brace position
until the aircraft comes to a complete stop, and
cabin stendants issue further instruction.
CAAC 2003/05
434

NON-SMOKING RULES ABOUT FLIGHT SAFETY
TURBULENCE
moking is prohibited not only on domestic
flights, but also in the ramp, bridge, and wait-
ing lounge in the Republic Of China.
Non-smoking areas include all non-smoking
seats, aisles and lavatories on international flights.
There is a smoke detector inside each lavatory.
Smoking will cause the detector alarm to sound.
This action not only disturbs all passengers but
also endangers flight safety.
urbulence results from thunderstorms,
heated air currents, wind shifts, and some-
times occurs in Clear Air Turbulence (C.A.T.).
Should trubulence be encountered:
1. Return to seat and fasten seat belt.
2. Hold onto armrest or seat back in the aisle.
3. Hold onto the handrail in the lavatory.

BAGGAGE LIMITATION

assengers may check in baggage free of
charge, subject to weight and quantity re-
strictions.
The best personal security is to pack your own
bags and never let them out of your sight until
you have them checked in at the airport. Restricted
items are prohibited from baggage.
One baggage suitable for placing in the closed
overhead bin or under passengers' seat maybe
carried into cabin, approximately within the di-
mensions of 56 cm x 36 cm x 23 cm, but not ex-
ceeding the total sum of dimensions 115cm,
weighting up to 5kg.
ELECTRONIC ITEMS
SEAT BELT
1 o avoid interference with aircraft naviga-
tion and communications systems, portable
telephone and electronic devices which are re-
motely controlled are prohibited through out the
The following devices are permitted to be op-
erated by passenger after aircraft reaches safe al-
titude. Portable voice recorders, portable self pow-
ered computers, recording typewriters and word
processors, hand-held calculators and electronic
games, electric shavers, and CD players/
walkmans.
There are no restrictions on use of hearing aids
and heart pacemakers.
T
o fasten seat belt simply insert the buckle
and adjust the length, lower the belt on the
torso as much as possible, then tighten the belt.
For safety, please don't fasten seat belt around
waist and don't put pillow or blanket between belt
and body except on a child.
